data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The distinction between genuine reliability gain and mere checklist compliance cannot be established within a single evaluation if the evaluation only samples the natural distribution of items; it requires out-of-distribution (OOD) adversarial probes. If the checklist is a surface proxy, it will track the right answer on the natural distribution by definition, making compliance indistinguishable from genuine causal capture without OOD interventions.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the checklist items are deductively linked to the outcome (i.e., the checklist is provably causally complete), then compliance IS the mechanism and the distinction is moot \u2014 no OOD probes are needed.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the checklist author explicitly disclaims causal completeness and frames the checklist as a surface heuristic, then compliance is the intended mechanism, and the distinction is again moot.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the single evaluation includes a sufficiently diverse set of natural items that the distribution spans both correlated and decorrelated surface\u2192outcome configurations, it may approximate OOD evidence without explicit adversarial probes.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A checklist that captures surface correlations rather than causal structure will perform reliably on the training distribution (where the surface cues align with the outcome) but will fail on adversarial items designed to break the surface\u2192outcome link. A single evaluation using only natural-distribution items cannot distinguish these two hypotheses because both the surface proxy and the causal model predict success on that distribution. Only by introducing items that decorrelate the surface cues from the latent outcome can the evaluation separate 'the checklist is causally complete' from 'the checklist happens to be causally complete on this distribution.' This means the evidence required to distinguish genuine gain from compliance-tracking is, by necessity, cross-distribution evidence \u2014 a single in-distribution evaluation is insufficient.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
